question_text: Why are pentahalides more covalent than trihalides?
answer_text: In pentahalides, the oxidation state is +5 and in trihalides, the oxidation state is +3. Since the metal ion with a high charge has more polarizing power, pentahalides are more covalent than trihalides.
final_answer: Therefore, pentahalides are more covalent due to higher oxidation state and polarizing power.

question_text: Bond angle in PH3 is higher than that in NH3. Why?
answer_text: In PH3, P is sp3 hybridized. Three orbitals are involved in bonding with three hydrogen atoms and the fourth one contains a lone pair. As lone pair-bond pair repulsion is stronger than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, the tetrahedral shape associated with sp3 bonding is changed to pyramidal. NH4+ combines with a proton to form NH3 in which the lone pair is absent. Due to the absence of lone pair in NH4+, there is no lone pair-bond pair repulsion. Hence, the bond angle in NH4+ is higher than the bond angle in PH3.
final_answer: Therefore, the bond angle in NH4+ is higher than in PH3 due to the absence of lone pair-bond pair repulsion.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of hybridization and molecular geometry.

question_text: Comment on the nature of two S-O bonds formed in SO molecule. Are the two S-O bonds in this molecule equal?

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating the hybridization and bond formation in SO molecule.

answer_text: The electronic configuration of S is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4. During the formation of SO, one electron from 3p orbital goes to the 3d orbital and S undergoes sp2 hybridization. Two of these orbitals form sigma bonds with two oxygen atoms and the third contains a lone pair. p-orbital and d-orbital contain an unpaired electron each. One of these electrons forms a p-p bond with one oxygen atom and the other forms a p-d bond with the other oxygen. This is the reason SO has a bent structure. Also, it is a resonance hybrid of structures I and II. Both S-O bonds are equal in length (143 pm) and have a multiple bond character.
final_answer: Therefore, both S-O bonds in SO are equal in length and have a multiple bond character.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of hybridization and bond formation.

question_text: Justify the placement of O, S, Se, Te and Po in the same group of the periodic table in terms of electronic configuration, oxidation state and hydride formation.
answer_text: The elements of group 16 are collectively called chalcogens. They have six valence electrons each with a general electronic configuration of ns2np4. They predominantly show an oxidation state of -2, but only oxygen shows this due to its high electronegativity. The heavier elements can show +2, +4, and +6 oxidation states. They form hydrides of formula HE, where E = O, S, Se, Te, Po.
final_answer: Thus, their placement in the same group is justified by their similar electronic configurations and oxidation states.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of periodic trends and chemical properties.

question_text: Why is dioxygen a gas but sulphur a solid?

difficulty_reasoning: Involves basic understanding of molecular structure and states of matter.

answer_text: Stability of an ionic compound depends on its lattice energy. The lattice energy of the oxide involving O2- is much greater than that involving O-. Therefore, the formation of O2- is energetically more favorable than O-.
final_answer: Thus, oxides with O2- ions are more stable than those with O- ions due to higher lattice energy.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of lattice energy and ionic stability.

subject: chemistry
question_text: List the uses of Neon and argon gases.
answer_text:
Uses of neon gas:
(i) It is mixed with helium to protect electrical equipments from high voltage.
(ii) It is filled in discharge tubes with characteristic colours.
(iii) It is used in beacon lights.
Uses of Argon gas:
(i) Argon along with nitrogen is used in gas-filled electric lamps. This is because Ar is more inert than N.
(ii) It is usually used to provide an inert temperature in a high metallurgical process.
(iii) It is also used in laboratories to handle air-sensitive substances.
final_answer: Thus, neon and argon gases have various important uses in electrical and industrial applications.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires basic knowledge of the applications of noble gases.
